# pragma: full docs for agents

> pragma is a web framework built for coding agents. An app is native HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript (never TypeScript) with a closed set of directives; a Rust CLI compiles, lints and validates it and answers every error with the file, the line, the rule and the fix. Pages ship prebuilt with only the JavaScript they use, and every form is a WebMCP tool by default.

This file has everything needed to build a pragma app: install, the loop, the app rules (AGENTS.md) and every doc. Index: https://pragma.leonavas.com/llms.txt. Each part is also a separate file under https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/.

## Install and create

pragma is one Rust binary. The installer supports Linux and macOS. Binaries for all platforms: https://github.com/leonavas/pragma/releases/latest. Node 22 or newer only runs `.server.js` files.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leonavas/pragma/main/install.sh | sh
pragma new my-app
cd my-app
pragma dev
```

Or build from source with Cargo:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/leonavas/pragma && cd pragma && cargo install --path core/cli/crates/pragma-cli
```

## Validate version and update

Validate the pragma version before you change code:

1. Run `pragma -V` to check the installed CLI version.
2. Compare that version with `.pragma/version` inside the app.
3. Run `pragma self-update` to update the CLI binary from GitHub Releases if the CLI is old.
4. Run `pragma upgrade` inside the app to update `.pragma/` (runtime, docs, `base.css`, `version`) if `.pragma/` is outdated.

```sh
pragma -V
cat .pragma/version
pragma self-update
pragma upgrade
```

## The loop

1. Validate the pragma version (`pragma -V` vs `.pragma/version`); run `pragma self-update` and `pragma upgrade` if outdated.
2. Read `AGENTS.md` in the app (the rules below), then the doc for the task in `.pragma/docs/`.
3. Write the code: one `.html` per page or component, plain JS, utility classes.
4. Run `pragma check --strict` and fix every error and warning at its cause, never around the rule.
5. Finish when `pragma check --strict` prints no problems. `pragma build` writes `dist/`.

## Contents

- [App rules (AGENTS.md)](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/rules.md): the rules every pragma app follows; read first
- [App structure](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/structure.md): where each file goes, pragma.json
- [HTML syntax](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/syntax.md): HTML directives ({path}, :, ., @, $) and blocks
- [Components](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/components.md): components, props, slots
- [State: script, actions, derived values, stores](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/state.md): script: state, actions, derived values, mount, stores
- [Routes and router](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/routes.md): pages, links, params, query, layouts (including nested), head tags
- [Data: load, server actions, skeleton, SSR](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/data.md): load, server actions, skeleton, SSR
- [Overlays: modal, alert, dropdown](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/overlays.md): modal, alert, dropdown
- [CSS](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/css.md): styles and theme
- [Utility classes](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/classes.md): every utility class
- [WebMCP: forms are agent tools](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/webmcp.md): forms as WebMCP tools, markdown for agents
- [npm packages](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/packages.md): npm packages: when and which
- [Performance](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/performance.md): performance defaults and budgets
- [Logs](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/logs.md): OpenTelemetry logs
- [pragma CLI](https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/cli.md): commands, self-update, upgrade, check rules, deploy

# AGENTS.md

A pragma app uses native HTML, CSS, and JS without a framework. Read the relevant file in `.pragma/docs/` before you change code.

## Version check

1. Compare `pragma -V` with `.pragma/version`.
2. If they differ, or if `pragma check` reports `app/core-outdated`, run `pragma upgrade`.
3. Run `pragma self-update` to update the CLI binary.

## Syntax

A page or component is one `.html` file: optional `<script>`, optional `<style>`, then markup.

- Top-level `let` declares state.
- A function defines an action (`@click="add"`) or a derived value (`{$total}` in HTML, `total()` in JS).
- `export let step = 1` declares a prop.
- `function mount(el) { …; return cleanup }` runs after mount.
- Import services from `'pragma'`: `import { shared, data, params, query, page, call, navigate, open, close, confirm, log } from 'pragma'`.
- `<style>` scopes to its component or page (`:global(…)` opts out only its argument).
- `{path}` inserts escaped text in text and attribute strings (`<p>Hi {$name}</p>`, `href="/shop/{p.id}"`).
- `:` binds a value (`:href`, `:disabled`). `.` toggles a class. `@` binds an event.
- `$` references a `<script>` name in HTML only (write `name` in JS).
- `@input="search"` passes `event`. `@change="toggle(task)"` passes only the listed arguments (paths, literals, `event`, `el`).
- Call store functions directly: `@click="shared.cart.remove(item.id)"`.
- Use tags for blocks: `<if v>`, `<else-if v>`, `<else>`, `<for x in v key=x.id>`, `<empty>`.
- `<c-x>` maps to `lib/components/x/`. `<p-x>` maps to `_components/x/` in the page folder or an ancestor.
- `routes/_layout.html` is the root layout (`<main data-page><slot></slot></main>`). Any subfolder can add `_layout.html` with `<slot></slot>` (no `<head>`, no `<script>`, no `.server.js`) to wrap routes in that folder and its subfolders.

## Rules

- Validate `pragma -V` against `.pragma/version`. Run `pragma upgrade` on mismatch or `app/core-outdated`.
- Use plain JS (ES modules). Do not use TypeScript, JSDoc types, or `console.*` (use `log.*`).
- Add npm packages only when the platform lacks the feature. Prefer plain JS ES modules (`packages.md`).
- Do not put HTML in JS. Do not mutate the DOM; assign a `let`.
- Write strict HTML. Close every non-void tag.
- Compute derived values in functions (`const total = () => …`). Do not write expressions in HTML.
- Read `data` inside functions only; it is undefined until `load` finishes.
- Put stores in `lib/state/`. Access stores only through `shared`.
- Do not write comments.
- Use descriptive names. Do not use vague (`tmp`, `data`, `info`) or short (`t`, `e`) names, except `i`, `j`, `k`, `id`, `ok`, `el`, `url`, `log`, and parameters of one-expression arrows.
- Keep the fixed folder structure. Do not edit `.pragma/` (run `pragma upgrade` to update it).
- Reuse existing components before creating new ones.
- Build overlays only with `c-modal`, `c-alert`, and `c-dropdown`.
- Load data with `load` in `.server.js` and render a skeleton.
- Use utilities from `classes.md`. Create a custom class only when a combination repeats 3+ times. Do not use inline `style`.
- Follow accessibility rules: name every control, add `alt` and labels, use one `<h1>`.
- Make every `<form>` a WebMCP tool: set `toolname` (`snake_case` verb_object), `tooldescription`, `name`, and `toolparamdescription` on each field. Add `notool` on login or password forms (`webmcp.md`).
- Run `pragma check --strict` before you finish. Fix all errors and warnings.

## To do X, read Y

| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| HTML syntax (`{}`, `:`, `.`, `@`, `$`, blocks) | `syntax.md` |
| File locations, `pragma.json`, `.pragma/version` | `structure.md` |
| Pages, links, params, query, root and nested layouts | `routes.md` |
| Page title, description, canonical, Open Graph, JSON-LD | `routes.md` (SEO) |
| Components, props, slots | `components.md` |
| `<script>`: state, actions, derived values, `mount`, stores | `state.md` |
| `load`, server actions, skeleton, SSR | `data.md` |
| Modal, alert, dropdown | `overlays.md` |
| Styles, theme | `css.md`, `classes.md` |
| Forms as agent tools (WebMCP), markdown for agents | `webmcp.md` |
| Performance | `performance.md` |
| Logs | `logs.md` |
| npm packages (install, selection) | `packages.md` |
| Commands, `check` rules, upgrade, self-update, deploy | `cli.md` |

Copy the doc example when unsure. If no doc covers a case, use the simplest code that passes `pragma check`.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/structure.md

# App structure

The folder structure is fixed. Do not create other top-level folders. Do not edit `.pragma/`.

```
<app>/
  AGENTS.md  CLAUDE.md
  pragma.json              { "name": "app", "lang": "en", "webmcp": true, "budgets": { "initialJsKb": 15, "routeJsKb": 10, "cssKb": 15 } }
  package.json             optional: npm packages in dependencies (packages.md)
  routes/
    _layout.html  _404.html
    index.html             page / (optional <script> and <style> at top)
    index.js               optional page script file instead of <script>
    index.server.js        optional server data and actions
    shop/
      _layout.html         optional nested layout for /shop/*
      [id].html            /shop/:id
      _catalog.server.js   private server helper
      _products.json       private data
      _components/<name>/  <p-name>
  lib/
    components/<name>/     <c-name>; starter ships modal, alert, dropdown
    state/<name>.js        stores (access through `shared`, never import)
    theme.css              tokens and global custom classes
  utils/                   pure functions
  public/                  static files (images, fonts, robots.txt, <page>.md for agents)
  .pragma/                 framework (runtime, docs, base.css, version); do not edit
```

## `pragma.json`

- `name` is required.
- `lang` sets `<html lang>` (default `"en"`).
- `webmcp` (default `true`) turns every `<form>` into an agent tool and enables `webmcp/*` rules (`webmcp.md`).
- `budgets` sets gzip kB limits: `initialJsKb` (all JS loaded by a page), `routeJsKb` (page JS outside `.pragma/`), `cssKb` (global CSS).

## `.pragma/` versioning

- `.pragma/version` records the `.pragma/` version.
- Compare `pragma -V` with `.pragma/version`.
- Run `pragma upgrade` to update `.pragma/` to match the CLI (`cli.md`).
- Run `pragma self-update [version]` to update the CLI binary (`cli.md`).

## File locations

| Item | Location |
|---|---|
| Page | `routes/<path>.html` (with `<script>`/`<style>`, or `.js`) + `.server.js` (same base name) |
| Root layout | `routes/_layout.html` |
| Nested layout | `routes/<folder>/_layout.html` |
| Server-only helper or JSON | `routes/<folder>/_name.server.js`, `_name.json` |
| Route-local component | `routes/<folder>/_components/<name>/` |
| Shared component | `lib/components/<name>/` |
| Shared state store | `lib/state/<name>.js` |
| Token, color, global class | `lib/theme.css` |
| Pure function | `utils/<name>.js` |
| Agent markdown page | `public/<path>.md` or `public/<path>/index.md` (`/` -> `public/index.md`; `webmcp.md`) |

## Rules

- A leading `_` makes a file or folder private (not a route). Only `_layout.html` and `_404.html` are special.
- Put at most one `<script>` and one `<style>` at the top level of a page or component `.html` (never in layouts). Or use `.js`/`.css` with the same base name, not both.
- Do not create `src/`, `pages/`, `styles/`, or `helpers/`.
- Put CSS in a component or page `<style>`, a component `.css`, or `lib/theme.css`.
- Naming: component folder uses lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; route param `[name]` uses letters, digits, `_`; store file uses a valid JS identifier.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/syntax.md

# HTML syntax

Pragma HTML uses a closed set of directives and block tags. Any other syntax is an error.

- `{path}` inserts escaped text.
- `:` binds an attribute or property.
- `.` toggles a class.
- `@` binds an event.
- `$` references a name from the owner `<script>` (state, prop, or function).

| Syntax | Target | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `{path}` | Text, attribute string | Inserts escaped text (`<p>Hi {$name}</p>`, `alt="Photo of {p.name}"`, `href="/shop/{p.id}"`). |
| `:<attr>="v"` | Element | Sets attribute (`:href`, `:disabled`, `:aria-current`). `false`/`null`/`undefined` removes it; `true` sets empty. `:checked` and `:selected` also set the DOM property. Never `:class`, `:style`, `:on*`. |
| `.<class>="[!]v"` | Element | Toggles the class. |
| `:show="[!]v"` | Element | Sets `hidden` when falsy. |
| `:model="$v"` | Input, select, textarea | Two-way binding (`$` or `shared` only). |
| `@<event>="fn"` | Element | Calls `fn(event)` on the owner (`@input="search"`). |
| `@<event>="fn(a, b)"` | Element | Calls `fn` with listed arguments only: paths (`task`, `$x`, `data.x`), `'text'`, numbers, `true`/`false`/`null`, `event`, `el`. |
| `@<event>="shared.cart.add(item)"` | Element | Calls a store function with the same argument rules. |
| `@open="id"` / `@close` | Button | Opens or closes an overlay (`overlays.md`). |

## Text: `{path}`

```html
<p>Hello {$name}, you have {$count} items</p>
<li>{task.title}</li>
<img :src="p.photo" alt="Photo of {p.name}">
<a href="/shop/{p.id}">{p.name}</a>
<label><input type="checkbox" :model="$done"> {task.title}</label>
```

- Use paths only (`$x`, `data.x`, `shared.x.y`, `params.x`, `query.x`, `page.x`, `<for>` variable). No expressions, calls, indexes, or `!`.
- `{$total}` calls derived function `total()` on each render.
- Output is always escaped text, never HTML. `null` and `undefined` render empty.
- Use `{}` in attributes to build strings (`alt="Photo of {p.name}"`). Use `:attr` for whole or boolean values (`:disabled="$atMinimum"`).
- Direct text inside `<code>` or `<pre>` stays literal (`<code>{x}</code>` renders `{x}`). Child elements still interpolate (`<pre><span>{$path}</span></pre>`). Directives, blocks, and components work inside `<code>`/`<pre>`.
- Write `\{` for a literal brace (`pattern="\d\{3}"`) and `&#36;{path}` for a literal `$` before `{path}` (`${` is an error).
- Do not use `{}` in `class` (use `.name="path"`) or in component props (use `:title="$title"`).
- Without `ssr`, prebuilt HTML omits dynamic text until boot. With `ssr`, the server renders it.

## Blocks

| Tag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `<if [!]v>…</if>` | Inserts or removes its content. |
| `<else-if [!]v>…</else-if>` | Follows `</if>` or `</else-if>` (any count). |
| `<else>…</else>` | Follows `</if>` or `</else-if>`. |
| `<for x in v key=x.id>…</for>` | Repeats per item; `key` must be stable and unique. |
| `<empty>…</empty>` | Follows `</for>`; renders when the list is empty. |

Write block paths without quotes: `<if page.loading>`, `<if !$open>`, `<for p in data.products key=p.id>`.

```html
<if page.loading>
  <p class="skeleton h-8"></p>
</if>
<else-if page.error>
  <p role="alert">{page.error.message}</p>
</else-if>
<else>
  <h1>{data.product.name}</h1>
</else>
```

## Values

Use `root.a.b` paths only. Do not use expressions, calls, indexes, or operators. Use `!` only in `<if>`, `<else-if>`, `:show`, and `.class`.

| Root | Value |
|---|---|
| `$x` | Owner state (`let`), prop (`export let`), constant, or function. |
| `data` | `load` result. |
| `shared` | Stores (`shared.cart.total`). |
| `params`, `query` | Path params and query strings. |
| `page` | `page.loading`, `page.error`. |
| `<for>` variable | Current loop item. |

Compute every derived value in a script or store function (`const total = () => …`). Value positions (`{}`, `:attr`, `.class`, `:show`, `<if>`, `<for>`) call the function with no arguments.

## Example

```html
<form class="flex gap-2" toolname="add_task" tooldescription="Add a task to the to-do list" @submit="add">
  <input name="title" class="flex-1 rounded-lg border border-line px-3 py-2" aria-label="New task" toolparamdescription="Task title, 3 to 80 characters" :model="$draft">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Add</button>
</form>
<p class="text-sm text-danger-600" role="status" :show="$error">{$error}</p>
<ul>
  <for task in $visible key=task.id>
    <li .line-through="task.done">
      <label><input type="checkbox" :checked="task.done" @change="toggle(task)"> {task.title}</label>
      <button type="button" aria-label="Remove {task.title}" @click="remove(task)">×</button>
    </li>
  </for>
  <empty>
    <li class="text-muted">No tasks.</li>
  </empty>
</ul>
```

## Owner

- The owner is the page or scripted component whose `.html` defines the element.
- `$`, `@`, and `:model` resolve against the owner. Slot content resolves against its caller.
- Root and nested `_layout.html` files have no owner; they read only `shared`, `params`, and `query`.

## Rules

- Each `<if>`, `<else-if>`, `<else>`, `<for>`, and `<empty>` must contain exactly 1 root element (not another block). Put directives on that element, not on the block tag.
- Write strict HTML and close every non-void tag. Do not use `<html>`, `<body>`, or `<template>`. Put at most one `<script>` and one `<style>` per file (`state.md`, `css.md`).
- `@submit` calls `preventDefault()` automatically. Every `<form>` is an agent tool (`webmcp.md`); read values with `new FormData(event.target)`.
- Pass `<for>` items as arguments (`@click="remove(task)"`). Without parentheses, the handler receives `event` (`@input="search"`). With parentheses, it receives only listed arguments (`@click="reset()"` receives none). Use `el` instead of `event.currentTarget` (events are delegated).
- Omit `$` in event names (`@click="increase"`). `:attr` takes a bare path (`:disabled="$atMinimum"`); use `title="Count {$count}"` without `:` for interpolated strings.
- Pass one bare path to block tags (`<if $hasTasks>` with `const hasTasks = () => tasks.length > 0`).
- Return `'true'` or `'false'` strings for `aria-*` states (`aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`), because boolean `false` removes the attribute.
- `:show` hides an element in the DOM; `<if>` adds or removes it. `autofocus` inside a newly inserted block receives focus.
- In dev, missing paths throw (except under `query`).
- Allowed markers: `data-page` (root layout `<main>`), `data-reload` (full-load `<a>`). Never write `data-c`, `data-tid`, `data-of`, `data-slot`, or `data-prop-*`.
- Do not write `data-*` attributes by hand (`html/data-attribute`). Bind `:data-x="path"` for multi-value style hooks (`[data-x=value]`), `.name="path"` for on/off states, and role/label/id for tests.
- `:text` is removed (`html/text-removed`); use `{path}` inside the element.
- Forbidden: inline `style` and `on*`, `:class`, `{{ }}`/`${ }` outside direct `<code>`/`<pre>` text (`html/interpolation`), legacy `state.`/`props.`, and foreign directives (`v-if`, `x-show`, `on:click`, `*ngIf`, `[disabled]`: `html/unknown-directive`).

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/components.md

# Components

Search `lib/components/` and `_components/` before you create a component.

| Tag | Folder | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `<c-name>` | `lib/components/name/` | Shared across multiple route folders. |
| `<p-name>` | `_components/name/` in the page folder or an ancestor | Used in one route folder only. |

To promote a `p-` component, move the folder to `lib/components/` and rename `p-` to `c-`.

```
name/
  name.html   required: optional <script> and <style> at top level, then 1 root element
              (not <template>, <slot>, or another component)
  name.js     optional: replaces <script>
  name.css    optional: replaces <style>; scoped automatically
```

- `<script>` defines state and behavior (`state.md`). `<style>` or `name.css` defines CSS.
- The build scopes every selector to the component root and its descendants. `button { … }` never matches outside.
- `:global(…)` opts out only its argument (`:global(html[data-theme="dark"]) .x` targets `.x` in dark mode; `:global(body.locked)` is global; see `css.md`).
- Selectors starting with `[data-c="name"]` stay as written.
- Using both inline `<script>`/`<style>` and external `name.js`/`name.css` triggers `html/duplicate-module`.
- `p-` names and styles are private to their folder. Two `<p-badge>` components in different folders get distinct `data-c` values and never share CSS.
- Do not select a `p-` component's `data-c` outside its `.css`. Select by class, role, or label.

## Props

Declare props in `<script>` with `export let name = default`:

| Caller writes | Script declares | Inside (`$x` in HTML, `x` in JS) |
|---|---|---|
| `label="Hi"` | `export let label = ''` | `'Hi'` |
| `start="10"` | `export let start = 0` | `10` (converted to the default's type) |
| `locked` / `locked="false"` | `export let locked = false` | `true` / `false` |
| `:product="p"` | `export let product = null` | The object itself, updated on each render |
| omitted | `export let step = 1` | `1` |

- Props are read-only (`js/prop-write`, including via `:model`). Copy a prop into a `let` to change it (`let count = start`).
- Object and array props are deeply read-only. In dev, mutating them throws `"props are read-only, also inside"`. Copy before changing (`let rows = files.map(file => ({ ...file }))`), or update through a store function or event.
- Passing an undeclared prop triggers `html/unknown-prop`.
- `class` is not a prop; it appends to the root element's classes.
- `id` is a normal prop (`export let id = ''`, then `:id="$id"`).
- Name props as one lowercase word (`label`, `step`); HTML attributes are case-insensitive.
- Components without a script use build-time props: `$label` replaces with caller text, `:x="path"` with caller path. Missing, `""`, and `"false"` are falsy.

## Example

`lib/components/counter/counter.html`:
```html
<script>
  export let label = ''
  export let start = 0
  export let step = 1

  let count = start

  const atMinimum = () => count - step < 0

  function decrease() { count -= step }
  function increase() { count += step }
</script>

<div class="inline-flex items-center gap-2" role="group" :aria-label="$label">
  <span class="text-sm text-muted">{$label}</span>
  <button type="button" class="btn" aria-label="Decrease" @click="decrease" :disabled="$atMinimum">−</button>
  <output class="w-8 text-center tabular-nums">{$count}</output>
  <button type="button" class="btn" aria-label="Increase" @click="increase">+</button>
</div>
```

Usage:
```html
<c-counter label="Steps of 5" start="10" step="5"></c-counter>
<for p in data.products key=p.id>
  <p-product-card :product="p"></p-product-card>
</for>
```

## Slots

```html
<c-modal id="about" title="About">
  <p>The body goes in the default slot.</p>
  <button slot="actions" type="button" class="btn" @close>Close</button>
</c-modal>
```

- `<slot></slot>` receives default children. `<slot name="actions">` receives `slot="actions"`.
- Filling a slot that does not exist is an error.
- Slot content belongs to its caller; `$` and `@` resolve in the caller's scope.

## Rules

- In a scriptless component, `@` calls the caller's function.
- State is per instance. A component script loads only on pages that use it.
- Do not put `.server.js` in components; load data in the page's `load`.
- Do not read or mutate a child's state. Pass props; let the child call its own action or a store function.
- Do not use `customElements.define` or shadow DOM. Build overlays with `c-modal`, `c-alert`, and `c-dropdown` (`overlays.md`).

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/state.md

# State: script, actions, derived values, stores

The top-level `<script>` of a page or component defines its state and behavior. Assign a `let` to update HTML (batched once per microtask). Do not use signals or manual renders.

| Top-level declaration | Role |
|---|---|
| `let draft = ''` | Instance state (`$draft` in HTML). |
| `export let step = 1` | Prop (`components.md`). |
| `function add() {…}` used as `@submit="add"` | Action. |
| `const saveLater = debounce(save, 300)` used as `@input="saveLater"` | Action (any top-level `const` holding a function works as a handler). |
| `const visible = () => …` used in `{}`, `<for>`, `:attr` | Derived value, recomputed on each render (call `visible()` in JS). |
| `function mount(el) { …; return cleanup }` | Runs external effects after mount (`el` is the component root or `<main data-page>`). |
| `import { shared, data, … } from 'pragma'` | Runtime services. |

`routes/tasks/index.html`:
```html
<script>
  import { shared, query, log } from 'pragma'

  let draft = ''
  let error = ''

  const visible = () => shared.tasks.items.filter(task => query.filter !== 'pending' || !task.done)

  function add(event) {
    const title = String(new FormData(event.target).get('title') ?? '').trim()
    error = title.length < 3 ? 'Use at least 3 characters.' : ''
    if (error) {
      if (event.agentInvoked) event.respondWith(Promise.resolve({ error }))
      return
    }
    shared.tasks.add(title)
    draft = ''
    log.info('task added')
    if (event.agentInvoked) event.respondWith(Promise.resolve({ ok: true, title }))
  }

  function toggle(task) {
    task.done = !task.done
  }
</script>

<form class="flex gap-2" toolname="add_task" tooldescription="Add a task to the to-do list" @submit="add">
  <input name="title" class="flex-1" aria-label="New task" toolparamdescription="Task title, at least 3 characters" :model="$draft">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Add</button>
</form>
<p role="alert" :show="$error">{$error}</p>
<ul>
  <for task in $visible key=task.id>
    <li>
      <input type="checkbox" :checked="task.done" :aria-label="task.title" @change="toggle(task)">
      <span>{task.title}</span>
    </li>
  </for>
</ul>
```

## Wrapped handlers

Bind functions returned by helpers (`debounce`, `throttle`, `once`) directly as top-level `const` handlers:

```html
<script>
  import { debounce } from 'es-toolkit/function'

  let draft = ''
  let saved = ''

  const saveLater = debounce(() => { saved = draft }, 300)
</script>

<input aria-label="Draft" :model="$draft" @input="saveLater">
<p>Saved: {$saved}</p>
```

If a top-level `const` handler does not hold a function, dev throws when the event fires.

## `mount(el)`

Use `mount(el)` for timers, observers, global listeners, measurements, and focus. Return a cleanup function.

```js
let now = Date.now()

function mount() {
  const timer = setInterval(() => { now = Date.now() }, 1000)
  return () => clearInterval(timer)
}
```

```js
let lines = 0

function mount(el) {
  const observer = new ResizeObserver(() => { lines = Math.round(el.clientHeight / 24) })
  observer.observe(el)
  return () => observer.disconnect()
}
```

- `mount` runs only in the browser and may be `async` (resolved function is the cleanup).
- Read from `el`; do not mutate `el`.
- Declare values used only inside `mount` (timer IDs, observers, DOM nodes) as `const` inside `mount`, not top-level `let`.

## Derived values

Compute derived values in functions: `$total` in HTML, `total()` in JS. Computing from state once in a top-level `let`/`const` triggers `js/stale-derived`. Reading a derived function without `()` in JS triggers `js/derived-call`.

```js
let count = 0
let doubled = count * 2            // js/stale-derived
const doubled = () => count * 2    // valid: `$doubled` in HTML, `doubled()` in JS

function check() {
  if (empty) return                // js/derived-call
  if (empty()) return              // valid
}
```

`let count = start` (from a prop) is valid when an action reassigns `count` later.

For per-item derived values, return row objects from a derived function (`{}` accepts paths only):

```js
const rows = () => items.map(item => ({ item, label: formatPrice(item.price) }))
```
```html
<for row in $rows key=row.item.id>
  <li>{row.item.name}: {row.label} <button @click="remove(row.item)">x</button></li>
</for>
```

Keep the original `item` reference (`row.item`) when mutating it. Spreading `{ ...item, label }` creates a copy that does not update the source.

## Services (`import { … } from 'pragma'`)

| Name | Use |
|---|---|
| `shared` | Stores (`shared.tasks.items`, `shared.tasks.add(title)`). |
| `data` | `load` result (`data.md`); undefined until `load` finishes. |
| `params`, `query`, `page` | Route params, query strings, `page.loading`, `page.error`. |
| `call(name, input)` | Calls a server action (`data.md`). |
| `navigate(url)` | Navigates via the router. |
| `open(id)`, `close(id)`, `confirm(id)` | Controls overlays (`overlays.md`). |
| `log` | Emits logs (`logs.md`). |

## Stores

Create stores in `lib/state/<name>.js`. Access them as `shared.<name>` in HTML and scripts.

`lib/state/tasks.js`:
```js
let items = []
export const persist = ['items']

const pending = () => items.filter(task => !task.done).length

function add(title) {
  items.push({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), title, done: false })
}
```

## Rules

- State uses a deep Proxy: `items.push(x)`, `task.done = true`, and reassignment all trigger renders (including from `await`, timers, and promises). Maps, Sets, Dates, and class instances are not tracked; reassign a new value.
- Define derived values as functions and call them in JS (`total()`). Do not copy derived values into a `let` (`js/stale-derived`, `js/derived-call`).
- Read `data` inside functions only (`js/top-level-data`). Wrap elements reading `data` inside the `<else>` of `page.loading`.
- Write `count` in JS, never `$count` (`js/dollar-in-script`).
- Keep page-only state in the page script. Use a store for shared or persisted state, and put actions shared by 2+ pages in the store.
- Store filters, tabs, and pagination in `query`, read by a derived function.
- `persist` saves listed `let` names to `localStorage`; use it only for preferences, drafts, and local-only data.
- Declare mutated top-level state with `let`, not `const` (`js/const-state`).
- Do not use `var`, destructuring `let`, or top-level `await`. Use `export` only for props (or `persist` in stores).
- Access stores only through `shared`; direct store imports trigger `js/store-import`.
- Do not mutate the DOM (`textContent`, `classList`, `setAttribute`). Call `addEventListener` only on `window` or `document` inside `mount`. Do not fetch data in `mount`. Do not build custom pub/sub.
- Do not use the legacy API (`export const state`/`actions`, `ctx.$`, `ctx.update`, `store()`): triggers `js/legacy-api`.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/routes.md

# Routes and router

| File | Route |
|---|---|
| `routes/index.html` | `/` |
| `routes/about.html` | `/about` |
| `routes/shop/index.html` | `/shop` |
| `routes/shop/[id].html` | `/shop/:id` |

- Every `.html` in `routes/` is a route, except names starting with `_`.
- Having both `x.html` and `x/index.html` is an error (`app/route-conflict`).
- `[name]` (file or folder) defines a path param. Static segments take priority over params. `[...rest]` is not supported.
- A page is an HTML fragment without `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>`. Top-level `<title>`, `<meta>`, and `<link>` move to `<head>` (see SEO).
- Read params as `params.id` and `query.filter` in HTML and scripts (`import { params, query } from 'pragma'`). Both are always strings.

## Root layout

`routes/_layout.html` wraps all routes:

```html
<head>
  <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
</head>
<header>
  <nav aria-label="Main">
    <a href="/" class="nav-link">Home</a>
    <a href="/shop" class="nav-link">Shop</a>
    <span>{shared.cart.count}</span>
  </nav>
</header>
<main data-page><slot></slot></main>
```

- `<head>` is optional and must come first. Its tags apply to every page and must be static (no `:` bindings, no `{}`).
- Include exactly one `<main data-page>` containing only `<slot></slot>`.
- The layout has no `<script>` and no `.server.js`. It reads only `shared`, `params`, and `query`. Use a component with `<script>` for behavior.
- `routes/_404.html` renders unknown routes. It has no `.server.js`.

## Nested layouts

Any subfolder in `routes/` can add `_layout.html` with `<slot></slot>` to wrap routes in that folder and its subfolders.

`routes/shop/_layout.html`:
```html
<div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-4">
  <aside aria-label="Shop menu">
    <a href="/shop" class="nav-link">All products</a>
    <a href="/shop/deals" class="nav-link">Deals</a>
  </aside>
  <section class="md:col-span-3">
    <slot></slot>
  </section>
</div>
```

- A nested `_layout.html` wraps the page inside the root `<main data-page>`.
- A nested `_layout.html` has no `<head>`, no `<script>`, and no `.server.js`.
- It reads only `shared`, `params`, and `query`.
- Include one `<slot></slot>` for the child route or inner layout.

## SEO and link previews

Put site-wide tags in `routes/_layout.html` `<head>`. Put page `<title>`, `<meta>`, and `<link>` at the top level of each page. A page tag replaces the layout tag with the same `name`, `property`, `http-equiv`, or `rel` (+ `hreflang`); new tags are added.

`routes/about.html`:
```html
<title>About · Shop</title>
<meta name="description" content="Who we are">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://shop.example/about">
<meta property="og:title" content="About">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://shop.example/about">
<h1>About</h1>
```

For server data, use `{path}` in `<title>` and `:<attr>` or `{path}` in `<meta>`/`<link>` with `data`, `params`, or `query`. Add `export const ssr = true` in `.server.js` so crawlers and link previews receive them in the first HTML.

`routes/blog/[slug].html`:
```html
<title>{data.post.title} · Shop</title>
<meta name="description" :content="data.post.summary">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://shop.example/blog/{params.slug}">
<meta property="og:type" content="article">
<meta property="og:title" :content="data.post.title">
<meta property="og:image" :content="data.post.image">
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Article",
  "headline": "{data.post.title}",
  "image": "{data.post.image}",
  "datePublished": "{data.post.date}",
  "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "{data.post.author}" }
}
</script>
<h1>{data.post.title}</h1>
```

`routes/blog/[slug].server.js`:
```js
export const ssr = true

export async function load({ params, request }) {
  return { post: await findPost(params.slug), url: new URL(request.url).href }
}
```

- Missing values keep the tag's static text or attribute. A `<meta>` without `content` or `<link>` without `href` is dropped.
- Put JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` at the top level of a page (never in a component); it moves to `<head>`.
- JSON-LD must be valid JSON (`html/json-ld`). `{path}` works inside strings with `data`, `params`, or `query` and `ssr`. The server JSON-escapes each value. A literal `{` in a string is `{`. Static JSON-LD needs no `ssr`. Other `<script type>` values trigger `html/script`.
- Do not put `canonical` or `og:url` in the layout.
- Do not place `<meta>` or `<link>` outside the page top level or root layout `<head>` (`html/head`).
- The router updates `<title>`, `<meta>`, and `<link>` on every navigation.

## Active link

- `<a href="/path">` (no query or hash) automatically gets `aria-current="page"` on the current route. Style `.nav-link[aria-current="page"]` in `lib/theme.css`.
- For query links (filters, tabs), bind `:aria-current` to a derived function that returns `'true'` or `false`:

```html
<script>
  import { query } from 'pragma'

  const pendingLink = () => query.filter === 'pending' && 'true'
</script>
<a href="?filter=pending" :aria-current="$pendingLink">Pending</a>
```

## Navigation

- Use `<a href>`. The router swaps `<main data-page>`, prefetches links, and keeps the root layout.
- Every navigation, including query-only changes, recreates page state.
- Navigate from JS after an action with `navigate('/shop?filter=sale')` (`import { navigate } from 'pragma'`).
- Force a full page load with `<a href="/logout" data-reload>`. Links with `target` or `download` also bypass the router.
- Do not use `<button>` + `navigate` instead of `<a>`. Do not use `location.href`, `history.pushState`, or `location` to read params.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/data.md

# Data: load, server actions, skeleton, SSR

| File | Export | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `x.server.js` | `load({ params, query, request, env, log })` | Return value becomes `data` in HTML and page `<script>`. |
| `x.server.js` | `actions.name({ input, params, env, log })` | Invoked via `call('name', input)` from `'pragma'`. |
| `x.server.js` | `ssr = true` | Renders `data` into the first HTML (SEO, link previews, LCP). |
| `_name.server.js` | helpers | Private to the folder; imported only by `.server.js` files. |

`routes/shop/[id].server.js`:
```js
import { findProduct } from './_catalog.server.js'

const likes = new Map()

export async function load({ params }) {
  return { product: findProduct(params.id) }
}

export const actions = {
  async like({ params, log }) {
    const total = (likes.get(params.id) ?? 0) + 1
    likes.set(params.id, total)
    log.info('product liked', { 'product.id': params.id })
    return { likes: total }
  },
}
```

`<script>` of `routes/shop/[id].html`:
```html
<script>
  import { data, params, call, log } from 'pragma'

  let sending = false
  let error = ''

  async function like() {
    sending = true
    try {
      data.product.likes = (await call('like')).likes
    } catch (failure) {
      log.error('product like failed', { 'product.id': params.id, 'exception.message': failure.message })
      error = 'Could not save right now.'
    } finally {
      sending = false
    }
  }
</script>
```

`data` is reactive: assigning `data.product.likes` updates the page.

## Skeleton (page with `load`, without `ssr`)

```html
<h1 class="text-3xl font-semibold">Shop</h1>
<if page.loading>
  <ul aria-busy="true" aria-label="Loading products">
    <li class="skeleton h-48 rounded-2xl"></li>
  </ul>
</if>
<else-if page.error>
  <p role="alert">{page.error.message}</p>
</else-if>
<else>
  <ul>
    <for p in data.products key=p.id>
      <li class="card">{p.name}</li>
    </for>
  </ul>
</else>
```

Keep titles, back links, and filters outside `<if page.loading>`. Match the skeleton shape to the final content.

## SSR behavior

With `ssr = true`, page and component scripts run once per request on the server so initial `let`s, props, and derived values appear in the first HTML. Keep browser-only code in `mount(el)` and actions.

| With `ssr`, in a page or component script | Server behavior |
|---|---|
| Top-level `let`, props, derived functions, slot content | Rendered into the first HTML |
| `data`, `params`, `query`, `page` | Read-only |
| `shared`, `call`, `navigate`, `open`, `close`, `confirm` | Throws; script deferred to browser |
| Top-level `window`, `document`, `localStorage` | Throws; script deferred to browser |
| Imports of npm packages or `.pragma/` | Skipped; script deferred to browser |
| Prop passed from a store | Deferred to browser |
| `mount(el)`, events | Browser only |

When a script is deferred to the browser, its `$x` bindings fill at boot while the rest of the page renders on the server.

## Rules

- Throwing in `load` sets `page.error` and returns HTTP 500. Return `{ product: null }` for not-found states.
- Put every write and every secret-using operation in a server action. Update `data` or a `let` after the call.
- Read `data` inside functions only (`js/top-level-data`). Without `ssr`, `data` is undefined until `load` finishes.
- Load data from `fetch` with secrets from `env`, a database via `env`, or `import products from './_products.json' with { type: 'json' }`.
- Default mode is no SSR: prebuilt HTML holds static content outside `<if>`/`<for>`, and `.pragma/boot.js` renders the skeleton.
- Enable `ssr = true` when crawlers, link previews, or data-bound `<head>`/JSON-LD tags need server data (`routes.md`).
- Do not fetch data in `mount` or client actions. Do not create `/api/...` routes. Do not return secrets from `load`. `env` exists only on the server.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/overlays.md

# Overlays: modal, alert, dropdown

Use `c-modal`, `c-alert`, and `c-dropdown` for all overlays. The runtime handles open, close, Esc, Back, focus, and scroll lock.

```html
<button type="button" class="btn" @open="about">About</button>
<c-modal id="about" title="About the app">
  <p>Content.</p>
  <button slot="actions" type="button" class="btn btn-primary" @close value="ok">Close</button>
</c-modal>

<button type="button" class="btn" @click="remove">Delete</button>
<c-alert id="remove" title="Delete project?">
  <p>This cannot be undone.</p>
  <button slot="actions" type="button" class="btn" @close value="cancel" autofocus>Cancel</button>
  <button slot="actions" type="button" class="btn btn-danger" @close value="ok">Delete</button>
</c-alert>

<c-dropdown id="account" label="Account">
  <a href="/profile">Profile</a>
  <hr>
  <button type="button" @click="logout">Log out</button>
</c-dropdown>
```

```js
import { confirm, call, params } from 'pragma'

async function remove() {
  if (await confirm('remove') !== 'ok') return
  await call('remove', { id: params.id })
}
```

| Component | Props | Slots | Closes on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c-modal` | `id`, `title` | default, `actions` | Esc, backdrop, ×, `@close`, Back |
| `c-alert` | `id`, `title` | default, `actions` | Esc, `@close`, Back |
| `c-dropdown` | `id`, `label` | default (`<a>`, `<button>`, `<hr>`) | outside click, Esc, `@close`, Back |

| JS (`import { open, close, confirm } from 'pragma'`) | Effect |
|---|---|
| `open(id)` / `close(id)` | Opens or closes the overlay. |
| `await confirm(id)` | Opens the overlay and resolves to the clicked `@close` button's `value`, or `'cancel'`. |

## Rules

- Back closes the top overlay, not the page. Overlays stack.
- Modal and alert lock scroll; dropdown does not. Focus returns to the opener.
- Put `autofocus` on the safe button in destructive confirmations.
- Open overlays only after a user click.
- Do not write `<dialog>` or `[popover]` by hand. Do not call `showModal()` or `window.confirm`. Do not store open state in a `let`. Do not use `role="menu"` or import `.pragma/overlay.js`.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/css.md

# CSS

Use utility classes (`classes.md`) first. Write a custom class only when utilities are not enough.

| File | Scope |
|---|---|
| `.pragma/base.css` | Preflight, layers, `.skeleton`, `[hidden]`, scroll lock. Do not edit. |
| `lib/theme.css` | Tokens and global custom classes (`@layer components`). |
| Component `<style>` or `<name>.css` | Scoped to that component (root and descendants). `:global(…)` opts out. `[data-c="<name>"]` stays as written (unique per folder for `p-`). |
| Page `<style>` or `<page>.css` | Scoped to that page's `<main data-page="…">`. |

Scoping appends `:where(…)` to each selector's last part, adding zero specificity. Write plain selectors (`button`, `.row:hover`, `li::marker`). Use `:global(…)` only for parts outside the component or page:

| Written | Compiled | Matches |
|---|---|---|
| `.row` | `.row:where(<scope>,<scope> *)` | `.row` inside this component only |
| `:global(html[data-theme="dark"]) .row` | `html[data-theme="dark"] .row:where(…)` | This component's `.row` in dark mode |
| `.list :global(.hit)` | `.list:where(…) .hit` | Any `.hit` inside this component's `.list` (including child components) |
| `:global(:root)`, `:global(body.locked)` | `:root`, `body.locked` | Global |

An outside ancestor alone needs no `:global`: `html[data-theme="dark"] .row` compiles identically.

## Tokens and dark mode

The starter includes theme-aware tokens (`bg-surface`, `text-ink`, `text-muted`, `border-line`) and classes (`.card`, `.btn`, `.btn-primary`, `.btn-danger`, `.dialog`).

```css
@layer tokens {
  :root {
    --color-primary-600: oklch(0.55 0.2 260);
    --color-brand: oklch(0.7 0.15 150);
  }
  [data-theme="dark"] {
    --color-brand: oklch(0.6 0.12 150);
  }
}

@layer components {
  .btn:hover { background: var(--color-primary-700); }
}
```

- `--color-<name>` and `--color-<name>-<shade>` generate `bg-<name>`, `text-<name>-<shade>`, and related utilities. Redefine `--color-primary-*` to change the brand color.
- Redefinable tokens: `--color-*`, `--font-{sans,serif,mono}`, `--radius-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--spacing`.
- Dark mode uses `[data-theme="dark"]` on `<html>`. Use theme-aware tokens (such as `bg-surface`), or pair palette colors with `dark:` (`bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900`).

## Theme toggle

```js
import { theme, setTheme } from '../../../.pragma/theme.js'

let dark = theme() === 'dark'

const label = () => (dark ? 'Light theme' : 'Dark theme')

function toggle() {
  dark = !dark
  setTheme(dark ? 'dark' : 'light')
}
```

Do not write `data-theme` or read `localStorage` for theme state. Use `.pragma/theme.js`.

## Custom classes

- Create a custom class only when the same combination repeats in 3+ places, or when you need state selectors or animations.
- Forbidden: inline `style="..."`, arbitrary values (`w-[37px]`), negative utilities (`-mt-2`), undefined classes, `!important`, ID selectors, external `@import`, and single-use custom classes.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/classes.md

# Utility classes

Generated by `pragma-css` (`cargo run -p pragma-css --example classes_doc`); do not edit by hand.

Closed subset of Tailwind v4: same names, same effect. Any class not listed here is a
`pragma check` error. No arbitrary values (`w-[37px]`), no negatives (`-mt-2`). Custom classes,
tokens and dark mode: css.md.

## Notation

`{a,b}` = alternatives; `{,-a}` = no suffix or `-a`; `{1..12}` = integers.

- `S` spacing (n × 0.25rem; `px` = 1px): `0 px 0.5 1 1.5 2 2.5 3 3.5 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 11 12 14 16 20 24 28 32 36 40 44 48 52 56 60 64 72 80 96`
- `F` fractions: `1/2 1/3 2/3 1/4 3/4`
- `C` colors: `white black transparent current {neutral,primary,danger,success,warning}-{50,100,200,300,400,500,600,700,800,900,950}`
- Opacity on any color: `C/{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,80,90}` (e.g. `bg-primary-500/50`)

## Variants

- State: `group-hover:` `hover:` `focus:` `focus-visible:` `active:` `disabled:` (`group-hover:` reacts to a parent with `group`)
- Theme: `dark:`
- Responsive, mobile first: `sm:` ≥40rem, `md:` ≥48rem, `lg:` ≥64rem, `xl:` ≥80rem, `2xl:` ≥96rem
- Combinable; each variant at most once, one breakpoint max: `md:hover:bg-primary-600`

## Layout

- `block inline-block inline flex inline-flex grid inline-grid contents hidden`
- `static fixed absolute relative sticky`
- `{inset,inset-x,inset-y,top,right,bottom,left}-{S,F,auto,full}`
- `z-{0,10,20,30,40,50,auto}`
- `overflow{,-x,-y}-{auto,hidden,clip,visible,scroll}`
- `visible invisible`

## Flex and grid

- `flex-{row,row-reverse,col,col-reverse}`
- `flex-{wrap,nowrap,wrap-reverse}`
- `flex-{1,auto,initial,none}`
- `{grow,shrink}{,-0}`
- `basis-{S,F,auto,full}`
- `grid-cols-{1..12,none}`
- `grid-rows-{1..6,none}`
- `grid-flow-{row,col,dense}`
- `col-span-{1..12,full}`
- `row-span-{1..6,full}`
- `gap{,-x,-y}-S`
- `items-{start,end,center,baseline,stretch}`
- `justify-{start,end,center,between,around,evenly}`
- `justify-items-{start,end,center,stretch}`
- `self-{auto,start,end,center,stretch,baseline}`
- `place-items-{start,end,center,stretch}`

## Spacing

- `p{,x,y,t,r,b,l}-S`
- `m{,x,y,t,r,b,l}-{S,auto}`
- `space-{x,y}-S` — space between children

## Sizing

- `size-{S,F,auto,full,fit}`
- `w-{S,F,auto,full,screen,fit,min,max}`
- `min-w-{S,full,fit,min,max}`
- `max-w-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl,2xl,3xl,4xl,5xl,6xl,7xl,prose,full,screen,fit,none}`
- `h-{S,F,auto,full,screen,dvh,svh,fit,min,max}`
- `min-h-{S,full,screen,dvh,svh,fit}`
- `max-h-{S,full,screen,dvh,fit,none}`

## Typography

- `font-{sans,serif,mono}`
- `text-{xs,sm,base,lg,xl,2xl,3xl,4xl,5xl}` — size with line height
- `font-{thin,extralight,light,normal,medium,semibold,bold,extrabold,black}`
- `italic not-italic`
- `leading-{none,tight,snug,normal,relaxed,loose}`
- `tracking-{tighter,tight,normal,wide,wider,widest}`
- `text-{left,center,right,justify,start,end}`
- `uppercase lowercase capitalize normal-case`
- `underline line-through no-underline`
- `tabular-nums`
- `whitespace-{normal,nowrap,pre,pre-line,pre-wrap}`
- `break-{words,all}`
- `truncate`
- `line-clamp-{1..3}`
- `list-{none,disc,decimal}`

## Color

- `{text,bg,border,ring,divide,fill,stroke}-C`

## Borders and effects

- `border{,-x,-y,-t,-r,-b,-l}{,-0,-2,-4,-8}`
- `border-{solid,dashed,dotted,none}`
- `divide-{x,y}{,-0,-2,-4,-8}` — border between children
- `rounded{,-t,-r,-b,-l}{,-none,-xs,-sm,-md,-lg,-xl,-2xl,-3xl,-full}`
- `ring{,-0,-1,-2,-4,-8}` — box-shadow ring; color with `ring-C`
- `shadow{,-2xs,-xs,-sm,-md,-lg,-xl,-2xl,-none}`
- `opacity-{0,5,10,20,25,30,40,50,60,70,75,80,90,95,100}`
- `outline-{none,hidden}`

## Interaction and accessibility

- `sr-only not-sr-only`
- `cursor-{auto,default,pointer,wait,text,move,not-allowed,grab,grabbing}`
- `pointer-events-{none,auto}`
- `select-{none,text,all,auto}`

- `transition{,-all,-colors,-opacity,-shadow,-transform,-none}`

- `aspect-{auto,square,video}`

- `group` — marks the parent for `group-hover:`
- `skeleton` — pulsing loading block (from `base.css`)

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/webmcp.md

# WebMCP: forms are agent tools

WebMCP is on by default (`"webmcp": true` in `pragma.json`; omitted means `true`). Every `<form>` is a declarative WebMCP tool. The browser registers the tool while the form is mounted and removes it when the form unmounts.

```html
<form toolname="search_products" tooldescription="Search the catalog by name or category" toolautosubmit @submit="search">
  <label for="query">Search</label>
  <input id="query" name="query" type="search" required toolparamdescription="Words to search for in product names and categories">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Search</button>
</form>
```

| Attribute | Target | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `toolname` | `<form>` | Required with `tooldescription`. Lowercase `snake_case` `verb_object` (`search_products`, `add_task`, `create_order`), unique per page. |
| `tooldescription` | `<form>` | Required with `toolname`. One sentence of 4+ words describing action and purpose. |
| `toolparamdescription` | input, select, textarea | Describes the expected input. Without it, agents fall back to `<label>` text, then `aria-description`. |
| `toolautosubmit` | `<form>` | Submits without user click. Use only on safe, reversible forms (search, filter, add). Never on delete, pay, buy, cancel, send, or transfer. |
| `notool` | `<form>` | Excludes the form (login, password, payment). Removed at build time. |

- Add `name` to every field (`type=submit|reset|button|image` exempt).
- Use native constraints (`required`, `type`, `min`/`max`, `<select>` options) to describe parameters.
- Use static strings only; do not use `:` bindings or `{}` in tool attributes.
- Without `toolautosubmit`, the browser fills the form and focuses the submit button for the user.
- With `"webmcp": false`, any tool attribute triggers `webmcp/disabled`.

## Result to the agent

`@submit="fn"` (no parentheses) passes the `SubmitEvent`. `event.agentInvoked` is `true` when an agent submits. Call `event.respondWith(promise)` before any `await`. Read fields from `new FormData(event.target)`, not `:model` state.

```html
<script>
  import { call } from 'pragma'

  let products = []

  async function search(event) {
    const query = new FormData(event.target).get('query')
    const reply = call('search', { query })
    if (event.agentInvoked) event.respondWith(reply)
    products = (await reply).products
  }
</script>
```

Return plain JSON (`{ products: [...] }`, `{ error: 'Use at least 3 characters.' }`). Respond with validation errors too so the agent can retry.

## CSS

`:tool-form-active` matches a form while an agent fills it. `:tool-submit-active` matches its submit button. `.pragma/base.css` styles both; override them in `lib/theme.css` or page `<style>`:

```css
form:tool-form-active { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary-600); }
```

## Check rules (`webmcp/*`)

Errors (broken tool):

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `webmcp/pair` | Provide both `toolname` and `tooldescription`, or neither. |
| `webmcp/name` | Use 1–128 chars from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -` in `toolname`. |
| `webmcp/duplicate` | Use a unique `toolname` per page (`<if>`/`<else>` branches count separately). |
| `webmcp/param-name` | Add `name` to every field in a tool form. |
| `webmcp/dynamic` | Use static text only in tool attributes (no `:` or `{}`). |
| `webmcp/notool` | Use `notool` only on `<form>`, never with `toolname`. |
| `webmcp/attribute` | Put `tooldescription`/`toolautosubmit` only on `<form>`, and `toolparamdescription` only on input, select, or textarea. |
| `webmcp/disabled` | Remove tool attributes when `"webmcp": false`, or set `"webmcp": true`. |

Warnings (errors with `--strict`):

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `webmcp/form-tool` | Add `toolname` + `tooldescription`, or `notool`. |
| `webmcp/name-style` | Use lowercase `snake_case` `verb_object` with at least one `_` (`search_products`). |
| `webmcp/description` | Write 4+ words in `tooldescription`. |
| `webmcp/param-description` | Add `toolparamdescription`, `<label>`, or `aria-description` to the field. |
| `webmcp/autosubmit` | Remove `toolautosubmit` from destructive or financial tools (`delete_`, `remove_`, `destroy_`, `pay_`, `buy_`, `purchase_`, `cancel_`, `send_`, `transfer_`). |

## Disable WebMCP

Set `"webmcp": false` in `pragma.json` to disable `webmcp/*` checks (existing tool attributes then trigger `webmcp/disabled`). Prefer `notool` on individual forms.

## Markdown for agents

Non-browser agents request `text/markdown`. Add a `.md` file in `public/` matching the route: `public/index.md` for `/`, `public/pricing.md` or `public/pricing/index.md` for `/pricing`. When `Accept` prefers `text/markdown` (quality >= `text/html`), the server returns that `.md` file; otherwise it returns HTML.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/packages.md

# npm packages

Add a package only when the platform cannot do the task. Check `Intl`, `fetch`, `crypto.randomUUID`, `URLSearchParams`, and `structuredClone` first.

## Install

```sh
npm i date-fns --ignore-scripts
```

- List every imported package in `package.json` `dependencies`. Importing an unlisted package is an error.
- Use any package manager (npm, bun, pnpm); pragma reads `package.json` and `node_modules/`.
- Exclude `node_modules/` from git.

## Import

```js
import { format } from 'date-fns'

let today = format(new Date(), 'PPP')
```

- Use a quoted module specifier; do not use template literals.
- Import named exports from the index or a subpath. The build tree-shakes each ES module package.
- Each package outputs `/assets/npm/<package>-<hash>.js` (`@date-fns/tz` -> `date-fns__tz`) with `modulepreload`. Shared chunks go to `/assets/npm/_*.js`. Package size counts toward page budgets.
- Avoid `import * as x from 'pkg'` and `import('pkg')` when possible; they bundle the whole package.
- `process.env.NODE_ENV` evaluates to `"production"` in build and `"development"` in dev.

## Supported packages

Client code supports plain JS packages (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, plus imported `.json`) using ES modules or CommonJS. CommonJS packages cannot be tree-shaken and ship whole; prefer ES modules.

| Unsupported on client | Error |
|---|---|
| TypeScript, JSX, `.vue`, `.svelte`, imported CSS or assets | `app/package` |
| `node:*` or Node built-ins (`fs`, `path`) | `app/package` |
| Importing an export the package does not provide | `js/import` |
| UI frameworks (React, Preact, Vue, Svelte, Solid, lit, jQuery, Alpine) | `js/import` |

In `.server.js`, all `package.json` dependencies and Node built-ins (`fs`, `node:*`) work without extra listing. A built-in name listed in `package.json` (such as `buffer`) bundles as a package.

## Recommended

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Format dates, numbers, currency, plurals, relative time | Native `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.PluralRules`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` |
| Date math (add, diff, start of month) | `date-fns`; time zones: `@date-fns/tz` |
| Form or payload validation | `valibot` |
| Fuzzy list search | `fuse.js` |
| Charts | `chart.js` (render into `<canvas>` in `.html`) |
| Debounce, throttle, group, sort | `es-toolkit` |
| Unique ID | Native `crypto.randomUUID()` |
| HTTP requests | Native `fetch` |

## Do not use

| Package | Reason | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `moment` | Large, no tree-shaking | `date-fns`, `Intl` |
| `lodash` | CommonJS; ships whole (~25 kB gzip) | `es-toolkit` |
| `axios` | Large; redundant | `fetch` |
| `uuid`, `nanoid` | Redundant | `crypto.randomUUID()` |
| HTML-building libraries (`marked`, template engines, UI kits) | HTML in JS is forbidden | Markup in `.html` |

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/performance.md

# Performance

Pragma optimizes builds by default: prebuilt HTML, `load` fetch started in `<head>`, per-route CSS (inlined in production when <= 14 kB gzip), per-page JS, link prefetch and Speculation Rules, 103 Early Hints, precompressed `.br`/`.gz` assets, hashed immutable assets, unused CSS stripped, and `pragma check` budgets.

## Rules

- Navigate with `<a href>`.
- Match skeleton shapes to the final content.
- Set `width` and `height` on every `<img>`. Add `loading="lazy"` below the fold. Store AVIF or WebP images in `public/`.
- Set `font-display: swap` on custom fonts. Avoid `<link rel="preload" as="font">` unless proven faster on slow 4G.
- Give `<for>` a stable `key`.
- Omit `.js` on pages without interaction.
- Keep heavy single-page code on that page. Load interaction-only code with `await import()` inside the action.
- Return only displayed fields from `load`. Run independent requests with `Promise.all`.
- Do not raise budgets in `pragma.json`; reduce code size instead.
- Do not import large modules in `lib/state/`. Do not fetch data in `mount`. Do not enable `ssr` by default.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/logs.md

# Logs

Pragma configures OpenTelemetry on client and server automatically.

- In page, component, and store scripts, import `log` from `'pragma'`.
- In `load` and server actions, use the `log` argument.
- In `utils/`, import `log` from `'../.pragma/log.js'`.

```js
import { call, params, log } from 'pragma'

let error = ''

async function save() {
  try {
    await call('save', { id: params.id })
    log.info('order saved', { 'order.id': params.id })
  } catch (failure) {
    log.error('order save failed', { 'order.id': params.id, 'exception.message': failure.message })
    error = 'Could not save.'
  }
}
```

| Level | Use when |
|---|---|
| `debug` | Diagnostics (shown in `pragma dev`; off in production unless `PRAGMA_LOG_LEVEL=debug`). |
| `info` | Business event. |
| `warn` | Recoverable problem. |
| `error` | Failure. |

## Rules

- Keep messages short and fixed. Put dynamic values in attributes (`order.id`, `exception.message`, `http.request.method`).
- Do not duplicate automatic logs: unhandled errors, navigation, fetch failures, request spans, and `traceparent`.
- In `pragma dev`, client `log.*` also prints to the browser console.
- Client logs send to `POST /_otel`. On static hosts returning 404 or 405, the client stops sending.
- Forbidden: `console.*`, logging inside loops or on every keystroke, and logging passwords, tokens, cookies, emails, or personal data.

---

Source: https://pragma.leonavas.com/docs/cli.md

# `pragma` CLI

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `pragma -V` | Prints the installed CLI version. |
| `pragma new <dir>` | Creates an app with the fixed structure. Warns and keeps existing files if `<dir>` is not empty. |
| `pragma dev [--port 5180] [--host 127.0.0.1]` | Runs the dev server with WebSocket live reload. Shows an overlay on build errors while valid pages keep working. Starts Node >= 22 when `.server.js` exists. Prints `app/core-outdated` first if `.pragma/` is older than the CLI. |
| `pragma check [--strict]` | Checks JS, HTML, CSS, budgets, accessibility, and WebMCP tools. `--strict` turns warnings into errors. |
| `pragma build [--allow-outdated-core]` | Builds `dist/`. Stops with `app/core-outdated` if `.pragma/` is older than the CLI (`--allow-outdated-core` overrides this). |
| `pragma serve [--port 3000] [--host 127.0.0.1]` | Serves `dist/` as in production. |
| `pragma upgrade` | Syncs `.pragma/` (runtime, docs, `base.css`, `version`) with the installed CLI version. Prints updated, added, or removed files. Never edits files outside `.pragma/`. |
| `pragma self-update [version]` | Downloads the latest or specified `pragma` binary from GitHub Releases, verifies `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and replaces the executable. |

Run `pragma check --strict` before you finish. Fix all errors and warnings.
Output format: `file:line:column error|warning [rule] message`.
Fix the root cause; do not work around a rule.

## Versioning and updates

- `.pragma/version` stores the version of `.pragma/` in the app.
- Compare `pragma -V` with `.pragma/version`.
- If they differ, or if `pragma check` reports `app/core-outdated`, run `pragma upgrade`.
- Run `pragma self-update [version]` to update the CLI binary.

## Rules

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `js/syntax`, `html/syntax`, `css/syntax` | Write valid syntax. Close every non-void HTML tag. |
| `js/html-in-js` | Remove `innerHTML`, `createElement`, `document.write`. Put markup in `.html`. |
| `js/console` | Use `log.*` (`logs.md`). |
| `js/jsdoc-types` | Remove TypeScript and JSDoc types. |
| `js/import` | Import only project files, `.pragma/`, and `package.json` dependencies (`packages.md`). Pass a quoted specifier to `import()` (`import('./chart.js')`), never a variable or `${}`. |
| `js/comment`, `html/comment`, `css/comment` | Delete the comment. Use clear names. |
| `js/vague-name` | Use descriptive names. Avoid generic words (`tmp`, `data`, `info`, `handler`, `util`), names ending in a digit, and names under 3 chars except `$ i j k id ok el ctx url log` and parameters of expression-body arrows. |
| `js/legacy-api` | Replace old API (`export const state`/`actions`, `export function mount`, `ctx.$`, `ctx.update`, `store()`). Use top-level `let`, functions, `function mount(el)`, and `export let` (`components.md`, `state.md`). |
| `js/prop-write` | Do not mutate props (including via `:model`). Copy into a `let` (`let current = start`). |
| `js/const-state` | Declare mutated state with `let`, not `const`. |
| `js/store-import` | Access stores through `shared` (`import { shared } from 'pragma'`, then `shared.cart`). |
| `js/component-script` | Follow script rules (`state.md`): no `var`, no destructuring `let`, only `export let` props (stores export only `persist`), no top-level `await`, only valid `pragma` imports, no `$`/`$pragma` declarations. |
| `js/top-level-data` | Read `data` inside functions (`const products = () => data.products`), not at top level. |
| `js/stale-derived` | Convert static derived values to functions (`const doubled = () => count * 2`), or update them in actions. |
| `js/derived-call` | Call derived functions in JS (`empty()`), not as bare values (`if (empty)`). |
| `js/dollar-in-script` | Write `x` in JS; `$x` is HTML only. |
| `html/legacy-syntax`, `html/unknown-directive` | Use pragma syntax (`syntax.md`). Replace foreign attributes (`v-if`, `x-show`, `v-bind:href`, `on:click`, `*ngIf`, `[disabled]`, `className`) with pragma forms (`<if path>`, `:show`, `:href`, `@click`). |
| `html/data-attribute` | Do not write `data-*` by hand. Use short forms (`{path}` instead of `data-text`), `:data-x="path"`, `.name="path"`, `aria-*`, or role/label/id. |
| `html/invalid-path`, `html/invalid-root` | Use `root.a.b` with a valid root (`syntax.md`). Close `{}` (`\{` for literal). Pass only paths, `'text'`, numbers, `true`/`false`/`null`, `event`, or `el` to events. Omit `$` in event names. Use bare paths in `:attr` and `<if>`. |
| `html/text-removed` | Replace `:text` with `{path}` inside the element (`<p>{$name}</p>`). |
| `html/block`, `html/block-single-root`, `html/for-without-key`, `html/misplaced-else`, `html/misplaced-empty`, `html/outside-template` | Follow block rules (`syntax.md`). |
| `html/unknown-name` | Declare the name at the top level of the owner script (`let x`, `export let x`, `function x()`). Layouts have no script. In `@click="shared.cart.x(…)"`, `x` must be a store function. |
| `html/unknown-prop` | Declare the prop in the component script (`export let name = default`). |
| `html/duplicate-module` | Use inline `<script>`/`<style>` or external `x.js`/`x.css`, not both. |
| `html/component`, `html/unknown-component` | Follow component rules (`components.md`). |
| `html/layout`, `html/title`, `html/head` | Follow layout and SEO rules (`routes.md`). |
| `html/class` | Toggle classes with `.name="path"`. Do not use `:class` or `{}` in `class` (`syntax.md`). |
| `html/interpolation` | Replace `{{ }}` and `${ }` with `{path}` (`syntax.md`). |
| `html/script`, `html/style-inline`, `html/on-inline` | Put at most one `<script>` (optional `type="module"`) and one `<style>` at the top level of a page or component `.html`. Put JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` only at the top level of a page (`routes.md`). |
| `html/json-ld` | Fix invalid JSON or unclosed `{` in JSON-LD strings. Use `{` for a literal brace. |
| `css/unknown-class`, `css/arbitrary-value` | Use classes from `classes.md` or custom classes per `css.md`. |
| `app/structure`, `app/route-conflict` | Follow structure and route rules (`structure.md`, `routes.md`). |
| `app/package` | Follow package rules (`packages.md`). |
| `app/pragma-json` | Fix `pragma.json` (`structure.md`). |
| `app/budget` | Reduce bundle size (`performance.md`). |
| `app/core-outdated` (warning; error in `pragma build`) | `.pragma/` differs from the CLI version. Run `pragma upgrade`. Do not edit `.pragma/` by hand. |

## Accessibility (`a11y/*`, warnings; errors with `--strict`)

| Rule | Fix |
|---|---|
| `img-alt` | Add `alt` to every `<img>`. Use `alt=""` for decorative images. |
| `accessible-name` | Give `<button>` and `<a>` text, `{path}`, `aria-label`, or `title`. |
| `label` | Associate fields with `<label for>`, wrap in `<label>`, or add `aria-label`. |
| `dialog-name` | Add `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to `<dialog>`. |
| `click-non-interactive` | Put `@click` on `<button>` or `<a>`, or add `role` and `tabindex`. |
| `heading` | Do not skip heading levels. |
| `single-h1` | Use one `<h1>` per page (`<if>`/`<else>` branches count separately). |
| `tabindex` | Use only `0` or `-1`. |
| `duplicate-id` | Use a unique `id` per page. |
| `iframe-title` | Add `title` to `<iframe>`. |
| `a-no-href` | Add `href` to every `<a>`. Use `<button>` for actions. |

`:<attr>` and `{}` count as setting the attribute (`:aria-label="task.title"`, `aria-label="Remove {task.title}"`).

## WebMCP (`webmcp/*`, active when `"webmcp": true`)

Every `<form>` is an agent tool (`webmcp.md`).
- Errors: `webmcp/pair`, `webmcp/name`, `webmcp/duplicate`, `webmcp/param-name`, `webmcp/dynamic`, `webmcp/notool`, `webmcp/attribute`. With `"webmcp": false`, any tool attribute triggers `webmcp/disabled`.
- Warnings (errors with `--strict`): `webmcp/form-tool`, `webmcp/name-style`, `webmcp/description`, `webmcp/param-description`, `webmcp/autosubmit`.

## `dist/`

| Path | Use |
|---|---|
| `client/` | HTML per route and assets. Deploy to static hosting when no `.server.js` exists. |
| `server/worker.js` + `wrangler.jsonc` | Cloudflare Workers (resolves param pages via manifest and serves `_404.html` with 404). |
| `server/node.mjs` | Run `node dist/server/node.mjs` (reads `PORT`, default 3000). |

Every server (`dev`, `serve`, Workers, Node) returns the matching `.md` from `public/` when `Accept` prefers `text/markdown` (`webmcp.md`).
